vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: learn-reflect
Version: 0.1.0

The 'learn-reflect' skill provides a structured methodology for an AI agent to document lessons learned and improve its own tools (self-annealing). The instructions in SKILL.md focus on root cause analysis, knowledge capture, and preventing task drift through plan logging. While the skill encourages the agent to modify its own scripts to fix bugs or add validation, this behavior is explicitly aligned with the stated purpose of system improvement and lacks any indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized access.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only 'learn & reflect' helper and its instructions, metadata, and requirements are coherent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the SKILL.md content: it is a knowledge-capture/reflection helper. It requests no binaries, env vars, or config paths — which is proportionate for a documentation/retrospective skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are detailed and focused on capturing actions, errors, root causes, and embedding ('annealing') fixes into systems. They ask the agent to include specific error messages, file paths, and commands from the session; they do not explicitly instruct reading arbitrary system secrets or exfiltrating data, but following the guidance could lead the agent to collect session logs, file contents, or modify files if the agent has permission. Ensure the agent only accesses relevant data and avoids including secrets when recording lessons.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. This minimizes disk writes and arbitrary code execution risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or config paths, which is appropriate given its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable (normal). Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (disable-model-invocation=false). Combined with the annealing guidance (which suggests updating tools/scripts), this could result in the agent making persistent changes if the agent account has write/exec permissions — that is a deployment/environment risk to manage, not a problem with the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and low-risk: it's a structured guide for recording lessons. Before installing, confirm how your agent is permitted to access files and make changes: if you don't want automatic edits, restrict the agent's file/write permissions or disable autonomous invocation. When recording lessons, avoid copying secret tokens, passwords, or sensitive config into saved notes or shared logs. Prefer saving annealing changes via version-controlled commits and review them before applying automated edits.
